heal_pokemon_at_counter.description: Initiates and completes the healing dialogue with Nurse Joy at the counter, ensuring no automatic B presses cancel the menu. Prints the button sequence.
heal_pokemon_at_counter.python_script:
import json

# Precise button sequence to talk to Nurse Joy and complete healing:
# 1. Press A to talk
# 2. Sleep 1500ms for "Welcome..."
# 3. Press A to advance
# 4. Sleep 1500ms for "We heal..."
# 5. Press A to advance
# 6. Sleep 1500ms for "Shall we heal..." and HEAL/CANCEL menu to appear
# 7. Press A to select HEAL
# 8. Sleep 5500ms for the healing animation and jingle
# 9. Press A to advance "Thank you..."
# 10. Sleep 1500ms for "We hope..."
# 11. Press A to finish conversation
# 12. Sleep 1000ms to exit text box

buttons = [
    "A",
    "sleep 1500",
    "A",
    "sleep 1500",
    "A",
    "sleep 1500",
    "A",
    "sleep 5500",
    "A",
    "sleep 1500",
    "A",
    "sleep 1000"
]

print(json.dumps(buttons))

history.commit_message: Define a custom tool to safely heal Pokémon at the counter by disabling the harness auto-advance and pressing buttons with precise sleep times.

navigate_overworld.description: Plans and generates a sequence of overworld movement button presses ('Up', 'Down', 'Left', 'Right') using a BFS pathfinder to navigate safely around obstacles, ledges, and trainers on Route 25, Route 24, and Cerulean City. Directly uses the pre-injected input_data variable for parameter access.
navigate_overworld.python_script:
import json
import sys

# Input data injected by the harness
# Structure: { "start_x": int, "start_y": int, "target_x": int, "target_y": int, "map_id": str }
input_params = input_data

start_x = int(input_params["start_x"])
start_y = int(input_params["start_y"])
target_x = int(input_params["target_x"])
target_y = int(input_params["target_y"])
map_id = input_params["map_id"]

# Map definitions
# Map dimensions and key collision elements
MAP_LIMITS = {
    "0_36": (40, 18), # Route 25
    "0_35": (20, 36), # Route 24
    "0_3": (40, 36),  # Cerulean City
}

# Defeated trainers act as solid obstacles.
TRAINER_OBSTACLES = {
    "0_35": {
        (11, 31), # Bug Catcher Cale
        (10, 28), # Lass Ali
        (11, 25), # Youngster
        (10, 22), # Lass
        (11, 19), # Bug Catcher
        (11, 15), # Rocket Grunt
    },
    "0_36": {
        (8, 4),   # Hiker Franklin
        (14, 3),  # Youngster
        (18, 5),  # Green-Vest
        (18, 8),  # Lass
        (23, 9),  # Hiker Nob
        (24, 6),  # Jr. Trainer
        (32, 3),  # Lass No.7
        (37, 4),  # Lass No.8
    },
    "0_3": {
        (31, 20), # Hiker NPC
    }
}

# Solid walls/ledges/water coordinates (hardcoded or known boundaries)
SOLID_COORDINATES = {
    # Cerulean City boundaries
    "0_3": {
        # Water/pool elements inside the city
        (14, 0), (14, 1), (14, 2), (14, 3), (14, 4),
        # Blue roof left building
        (18, 24), (19, 24), (20, 24), (21, 24), (22, 24), (23, 24),
        (18, 25), (19, 25), (20, 25), (21, 25), (22, 25), (23, 25),
        # Blue roof right building
        (28, 24), (29, 24), (30, 24), (28, 25), (29, 25), (30, 25),
        # Gym walls
        (29, 19), (29, 20), (31, 19), (31, 20), (30, 18),
        # Southern ledges (cannot walk up across them)
        (9, 17), (10, 17), (11, 17), (12, 17), (13, 17), (14, 17),
        (15, 17), (16, 17), (17, 17), (18, 17), (20, 17), (21, 17),
        (22, 17), (23, 17), (24, 17), (25, 17), (26, 17), (27, 17),
    }
}

width, height = MAP_LIMITS.get(map_id, (40, 40))

def is_passable(x, y):
    if x < 0 or x >= width or y < 0 or y >= height:
        return False
    # Check defeated trainer obstacles
    if map_id in TRAINER_OBSTACLES and (x, y) in TRAINER_OBSTACLES[map_id]:
        return False
    # Check general solid coordinates
    if map_id in SOLID_COORDINATES and (x, y) in SOLID_COORDINATES[map_id]:
        return False
    # Route 24 (Nugget Bridge) strictly restricts Column 10 & 11 between Y=10 and Y=34 to stay on the bridge
    if map_id == "0_35" and 10 <= y <= 34:
        if x != 10 and x != 11:
            return False
    return True

# BFS Implementation
queue = [[(start_x, start_y)]]
visited = {(start_x, start_y)}

path = None
while queue:
    curr_path = queue.pop(0)
    curr_x, curr_y = curr_path[-1]
    
    if curr_x == target_x and curr_y == target_y:
        path = curr_path
        break
        
    for dx, dy, direction in [(0, -1, 'Up'), (0, 1, 'Down'), (-1, 0, 'Left'), (1, 0, 'Right')]:
        nx, ny = curr_x + dx, curr_y + dy
        if (nx, ny) not in visited and is_passable(nx, ny):
            visited.add((nx, ny))
            queue.append(curr_path + [(nx, ny)])

if path is None:
    print(json.dumps([]))
    sys.exit(0)

# Translate coordinates into buttons
buttons = []
for i in range(len(path) - 1):
    x1, y1 = path[i]
    x2, y2 = path[i+1]
    if x2 > x1:
        buttons.append('Right')
    elif x2 < x1:
        buttons.append('Left')
    elif y2 > y1:
        buttons.append('Down')
    elif y2 < y1:
        buttons.append('Up')

print(json.dumps(buttons))

history.commit_message: Initial definition of the navigate_overworld custom tool.
Corrected tool parameter input mechanism to read from pre-injected input_data global variable instead of sys.stdin.
Redefined navigate_overworld tool to correctly account for solid structures in Cerulean City and the Nugget Bridge layout, preventing collisions.
Updated navigate_overworld is_passable logic to strictly restrict Route 24 bridge corridor (Rows 10-34) to Columns 10 and 11, preventing collisions with side walls and water.
